I will keep this year simple and steady. In Quzhou County, the crop I trust most is the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because I know the land, I know the timing, and it spreads my risk across the whole year. At my age, I would not choose crops that need too much fine management or too much hand labor. I will keep the same land in two seasons: first I will carry the winter wheat through spring and early summer, then after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will use improved seed I can rely on, put on moderate fertilizer instead of chasing very high yield, irrigate when the crop truly needs it, and keep pesticide use limited to the times when pests or disease are likely enough to threaten the crop. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me to manage than deep ploughing, while still giving me a workable seedbed. My goal is not the highest possible output; my goal is a stable harvest with work I can still handle myself.
